h1:
Where to Stay in Pattaya?
10 Hotels We Actually Reviewed
Prices Compared on 3 Sites!
heroSub: 10 Pattaya hotels picked across every price tier — 5-star beachfront resorts and pool villas down to a cracking-value capsule hostel, covering the key areas: Central Pattaya, Pratamnak Hill, Naklua and Na Jomtien. From THB 700–18,000/night.
introH2: 🏙️ Why does choosing the right area in Pattaya matter so much?
introHtml: Pattaya's areas feel wildly different from one another — Central Pattaya Beach is the buzzing heart of town, next to CentralFestival mall, the beach, restaurants and nightlife all within walking distance · Pratamnak Hill is a quieter headland to the south with beachfront resorts and boutiques on the slope · Naklua / Wong Amat Beach to the north is calmer, with beachfront family resorts · while Na Jomtien further south is a long, quiet beach for a private getaway · Plenty of people book without checking the area and then spend all day shuttling back and forth by songthaew, losing precious sightseeing time · This guide rounds up 10 Pattaya hotels we've actually read the reviews for, across every tier — from beachfront resorts to a value capsule hostel, with prices compared on 3 sites and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Pattaya has no metro. The main way to get around town is the songthaew (red truck) that loops along Beach Road and Pattaya 2nd Road from THB 10, plus Grab and motorbike rental · From Bangkok it's about a 2-hour drive or van/bus; from U-Tapao Airport (UTP) around 40 minutes, from Suvarnabhumi about 1.5–2 hours · The key areas in this guide: Central Pattaya Beach — next to CentralFestival, the beach, Walking Street and nightlife (Hilton, Somerset, Wave, Vista) · Pratamnak Hill — a quiet southern headland with resorts and boutiques on the slope (InterContinental, Cross) · Naklua / Wong Amat Beach — quieter north side with beachfront resorts (Centara Grand Mirage, Cape Dara) · Na Jomtien — a long, quiet beach to the south (Veranda MGallery).

entries.name: Centara Grand Mirage Beach Resort
tags: 🌊 Lost World theme + on-site water park
entries.addr: 277 Moo 5, Naklua, Wong Amat Beach, Pattaya
entries.storyHtml: Centara Grand Mirage is the most-reviewed resort in this guide — over 2,137 reviews, scoring 9.1 · What reviewers mention most is the on-site Lost World–themed water park kids can splash in all day, the private Wong Amat Beach (quieter than Central Pattaya), and family rooms that sleep several children · It's a big resort that just works for families with young kids · Reviews are honest that it gets crowded and lively in high season, so it's not the pick if you want pure quiet.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Travelling as a family, choose a Family Suite or Family Residence that sleeps several kids, and hit the water park early before the late-morning crowds.
pros: On-site Lost World water park — kids splash all day (from reviews)
On private Wong Amat Beach, quieter than Central Pattaya
Family rooms sleep several kids · most reviewed at 2,137
Spacious sea-facing rooms, full family facilities
cons: Big, lively resort — crowded and noisy in high season
Not the pick if you want a pure, private quiet stay

entries.name: Hilton Pattaya
tags: 🛍️ Lift straight down to mall and beach
entries.addr: 333/101 Moo 9, Nong Prue, atop CentralFestival Pattaya Beach
entries.storyHtml: Hilton Pattaya is a beachfront luxury hotel right in town where every room starts on the 19th floor or higher, scoring 9.2 from 1,270 reviews · What reviewers rave about most: every room faces the sea with a balcony, the lift drops you straight into CentralFestival mall and across the road is the beach · There's a sky-high infinity pool and the Horizon Rooftop Bar on the 34th floor with 270-degree bay views · Ideal if you want sea views and convenience in one spot · Reviews do flag that it isn't cheap and the area is lively with nighttime noise.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Every room is sea-view, but ask for floor 25+ to catch the full sweep of Pattaya Bay — and head up to Horizon at sunset for the best views of the day.
pros: Every room is sea-view with a balcony (304 rooms, floors 19–34)
Lift straight down to CentralFestival mall and the beach (from reviews)
Sky-high infinity pool and Horizon Rooftop with bay views
High score of 9.2 from a large 1,270 reviews
cons: Pricier than typical Central Pattaya hotels
Central Pattaya is lively with street and nightlife noise at night

entries.name: Somerset Pattaya
tags: 🍳 Rooms with kitchens, great for long stays
entries.addr: 528 Moo 10, Pattaya 2 Road, Nongprue, Central Pattaya
entries.storyHtml: Somerset Pattaya is the most-reviewed property in this guide — over 2,642 reviews, scoring 9.3 · Reviewers most often mention the spacious rooms with kitchens that suit families and longer stays, the 23rd-floor infinity pool with sea views, and a pirate-themed water park for the kids · It sits opposite CentralFestival, an easy walk to the mall and beach · Great for families and multi-night stays who want space and a kitchen · Reviews note it costs more than typical chain hotels in the area and that breakfast still has room to improve.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For a group or long stay, the Studio Executive or Two-Bedroom units with a kitchen and washer work out better value than booking multiple rooms.
pros: Spacious rooms with kitchens — great for families and long stays (from reviews)
23rd-floor infinity pool and a pirate-themed kids' water park
Opposite CentralFestival, walk to mall and beach
High score 9.3 · most reviewed at 2,642
cons: Costs more than typical chain hotels in Central Pattaya
Breakfast is the point reviews say could improve

entries.name: Cross Pattaya Pratamnak
entries.addr: 286/4 Moo 12, Kasetsin Road, Pratamnak Hill, Pattaya
entries.storyHtml: Cross Pattaya Pratamnak is the design boutique with the highest score in this group on Pratamnak Hill — 9.4 from 352 reviews · Reviewers highlight the modern-colonial design that's photogenic throughout, sea-view rooms with balconies, and a salt-water pool and spa in the quiet of Pratamnak Hill · Starting prices are more accessible than the beachfront resorts, and it's a newer property (opened 2022) · Great for couples and anyone who wants a stylish hotel somewhere calm · Reviews are honest that you can't walk to the beach or nightlife so you'll need a car, and that room soundproofing isn't as good as it should be.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Bump up to a Luxury Ocean View for balcony views over Pattaya Bay, and grab a Grab down to Pratamnak Beach or into town easily.
pros: Highest score in this guide at 9.4 (from reviews)
Photogenic modern-colonial design throughout
Sea-view rooms with balconies · salt-water pool and spa, somewhere quiet
More accessible pricing than beachfront resorts · newer (2022)
cons: On the hill — can't walk to beach or nightlife, you'll need a car
Room-to-room soundproofing isn't as good as it should be (from reviews)

entries.name: InterContinental Pattaya Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Pratamnak Hill · south Pattaya · private beach
tags: 🏖️ Quiet private beach on the headland
entries.addr: 437 Phra Tamnak Road, Bang Lamung, Pratamnak Hill, Pattaya
entries.storyHtml: InterContinental Pattaya Resort is a beachfront luxury resort on Pratamnak Hill built around quiet and a private beach, scoring 8.9 from 567 reviews · Reviewers mention the 14-rai tropical garden sloping down to the sea, a small private beach, and three garden pools with a Kids' Club · It's only a 10–15 minute drive from Walking Street, yet inside it feels like an escape from the city · Great for couples and families on a relaxing trip · Reviews are honest that the beach is smaller than in the photos and you depend on a car to reach town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If budget allows, go for the Classic Ocean View — reviewers say the bay view from the balcony is worth the difference — and head to the seaside Infiniti restaurant at sunset.
pros: Quiet private beach on the headland, lush tropical garden (from reviews)
3 garden pools and a Kids' Club, family-friendly
Spacious ~51 sqm rooms with garden- or sea-view balconies
Close enough to town for a 10–15 minute drive to Walking Street
cons: Private beach is smaller than promo photos — better for lounging than swimming
On the hill, you depend on a car for town — not for walk-to-nightlife travellers

entries.name: Cape Dara Resort
tags: 🏖️ Private beach on the Naklua headland
entries.addr: 256 Dara Beach, Soi 20, Pattaya-Naklua Road, Naklua, Pattaya
entries.storyHtml: Cape Dara Resort is a beachfront resort on the Naklua headland where every room faces the sea, scoring 8.7 from 1,256 reviews · Reviewers mention the full Pattaya Bay views from the rooms and the sky infinity pool, plus a private beach in Naklua that's quieter than Central Pattaya · Prices tend to be more accessible than the big luxury chains in the same class · Great if you want sea views and quiet on a lighter budget · Reviews are honest that the beach has some rocks, parts of the building are showing their age, and you'll need a car to reach town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a high-floor Cape Premium Sea View for the widest bay view, and hit the sky pool in the late afternoon for sunset.
pros: Every room is sea-view with a balcony · sky infinity pool (from reviews)
Private beach on the Naklua headland, quieter than Central Pattaya
Usually better value than the big luxury chains in the same class
Plenty of reviews at 1,256 · good for couples and families
cons: The beach has some rocks and parts of the building are dated (from reviews)
In Naklua, you'll need a car to reach Central Pattaya

entries.name: Veranda Resort Pattaya Na Jomtien MGallery
entries.addr: 211 Moo 1, Na Jomtien, Bang Lamung, Pattaya
entries.storyHtml: Veranda Resort Pattaya MGallery is a design resort on Na Jomtien Beach in the MGallery Collection, scoring 8.7 from 524 reviews · Reviewers mention the infinity pool whose edge meets the sea, the quiet private Na Jomtien beach, and the striking, photogenic architecture · Great for couples and families who want a private stretch of sea in calm surroundings · Reviews are honest that Na Jomtien is far from town so you can't walk to nightlife, and that being open for years means some rooms feel aged and service can be inconsistent at times.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pick an Ocean Front Room for a direct sea view, and have a car or Grab ready if you plan to eat off-site, since the location is fairly far from town.
pros: Infinity pool meeting the sea and a private Na Jomtien beach (from reviews)
Striking design architecture in the MGallery Collection
Quiet and private — great for couples and families
Direct sea-view rooms and a Pool Suite for a private pool
cons: Na Jomtien is far from town — you can't walk to nightlife
Open for years, so some rooms feel aged and service is inconsistent at times

entries.name: Wave Hotel Pattaya
tags: 🛍️ Walk to mall and Walking Street
entries.addr: 310/3 Beach Road, Nong Prue, Central Pattaya beachfront road
entries.storyHtml: Wave Hotel Pattaya is a tiny 18-room Art Deco boutique on Beach Road with the highest score in this guide — 9.5 · Reviewers highlight the distinctive Art Deco design, every room being sea-view, and the close, personal service of a small hotel in the Sukosol group · It's right in the middle of Central Pattaya, an easy walk to the mall and Walking Street · Great for anyone who wants a stylish hotel and personal service · Reviews are honest that with just 18 rooms the pool is small and facilities aren't full-resort, and the area gets noisy at night · Few reviews so far (92) but the score is consistently high.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pick a Sunset Room or Ocean View Suite with a balcony facing the bay — the sunset view is the highlight reviewers mention.
pros: Distinctive Art Deco design, every room sea-view (from reviews)
Close, boutique-style service in an 18-room Sukosol hotel
Central Pattaya location, walk to mall and Walking Street
Highest score in this guide at 9.5, consistently
cons: Just 18 rooms — small pool, facilities aren't full-resort
Few reviews so far (92), and Central Pattaya is noisy at night

entries.name: Nonze Hostel
tags: 🛏️ A/C capsules with private sliding doors
🏖️ On Beach Road by the sea
entries.addr: 183/6 Beach Road, Moo 10, Nongprue, South Pattaya · Beach Road
entries.storyHtml: Nonze Hostel is the most-reviewed property in this guide with 4,074 reviews, and a high 9.2 — remarkably high for a hostel · Reviewers mention the air-conditioned capsules with private sliding doors, reading lights, power sockets and lockers — cleaner and more private than a typical hostel — plus a rooftop with Pattaya Bay views · It's on Beach Road, an easy walk to Walking Street and the beach, from just THB 700 · Great for budget travellers who can handle some entertainment-district noise and shared bathrooms.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Travelling as a pair or group, the Twin or Capsule Suite is more private at still-great value, and head up to the rooftop in the evening for the bay view.
pros: Cheapest in this guide at THB 700 · on Beach Road by the sea
A/C capsules with private sliding doors — clean and private (from reviews)
Rooftop with Pattaya Bay view · walk to Walking Street and beach
Most reviewed in this guide at 4,074, high score 9.2
cons: In the entertainment district — can be noisy at night, not for quiet-seekers
Dorms use shared bathrooms, not for families with young kids

entries.name: Hotel Vista Pattaya
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Central Pattaya · 2 min walk to beach
entries.addr: 196 Pattaya Road, Soi 4, Nong Prue, Central Pattaya
entries.storyHtml: Hotel Vista Pattaya is a budget-friendly modern hotel that's among the best value in Central Pattaya, scoring 8.5 from 1,865 reviews · Reviewers mention the 30-metre salt-water pool that punches above its price, the modern-design rooms, and a location just a 2-minute walk to Pattaya Beach and near the nightlife · From just THB 1,200 you get a vibe and facilities hard to find at this price point · Great for budget travellers who want a good room and a smart pool in town · It's not a private-beach resort, but it delivers strong value in Central Pattaya.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Bump up to Club Luxx for lounge access with afternoon snacks and drinks — better value than heading out for a snack.
pros: 30-metre salt-water pool that punches above its price (from reviews)
Modern-design rooms · 2-minute walk to Pattaya Beach
From THB 1,200 — excellent value in Central Pattaya
Plenty of reviews at 1,865 · near nightlife and the mall
cons: Not a private-beach resort — rooms aren't sea-view
In the middle of Central Pattaya, with noise and crowds at times

adviceTitle: How to pick the right Pattaya hotel for you

advice.head: Tight budget, best value
advice.bodyHtml: → Nonze Hostel THB 700, capsule hostel on Beach Road · or Hotel Vista Pattaya THB 1,200, a modern hotel with a salt-water pool in Central Pattaya

advice.head: Family trip with kids
advice.bodyHtml: → Centara Grand Mirage THB 4,800 with an on-site Lost World water park · or Somerset Pattaya THB 2,400 with kitchens and a water park, opposite the mall

advice.head: Special luxury sea-view trip
advice.bodyHtml: → Hilton Pattaya THB 4,500, every room sea-view in town, scoring 9.2 · or InterContinental Pattaya Resort THB 6,500, a private beach on Pratamnak Hill

advice.head: Quiet stay, away from the buzz
advice.bodyHtml: → InterContinental Pattaya Resort THB 6,500, private Pratamnak beach · or Veranda MGallery THB 4,200, a design resort on Na Jomtien Beach

advice.head: Stylish design hotel
advice.bodyHtml: → Cross Pattaya Pratamnak THB 2,500, a modern-colonial boutique scoring 9.4 · or Wave Hotel Pattaya THB 2,800, an Art Deco boutique with every room sea-view

advice.head: Beachfront resort with sea views
advice.bodyHtml: → Cape Dara Resort THB 3,500, a Naklua beachfront with every room sea-view · or Veranda MGallery THB 4,200, an infinity pool meeting the sea at Na Jomtien

advice.head: Close to the beach, mall and nightlife
advice.bodyHtml: → Hilton Pattaya THB 4,500, atop CentralFestival by the beach · or Wave Hotel Pattaya THB 2,800, on Beach Road, walk to Walking Street

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting rates and may change by date and season — always check live prices and compare 3 sites before booking · Pattaya room rates swing a lot by season and weekday vs. weekend; in high season (November–February), long weekends, New Year and Songkran, prices rise and rooms sell out fast, so book 2–4 weeks ahead or more · Pattaya has no metro — get around town by songthaew (red truck), Grab or motorbike rental; it's about 40 minutes from U-Tapao Airport into town · Scores and standout factors come from reading real guest reviews, not from staying ourselves. faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Pattaya hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in Pattaya as a tourist?
faq.a: It depends on your style · Central Pattaya Beach suits people who want the buzz — next to CentralFestival mall, the beach, restaurants and nightlife within walking distance (Hilton, Somerset, Wave, Vista, Nonze) · Pratamnak Hill is a quiet southern headland with resorts and boutiques on the slope (InterContinental, Cross) · Naklua / Wong Amat Beach is the quieter north side with beachfront resorts (Centara Grand Mirage, Cape Dara) · Na Jomtien is a long, quiet beach to the south for a private getaway (Veranda MGallery)

faq.q: ❓ How much do Pattaya hotels cost?
faq.a: Prices vary widely: capsule hostels start around THB 700/night · modern hotels and 3–4 star chains around THB 1,200–2,900 · boutiques and serviced apartments around THB 2,400–4,500 · beachfront resorts and 5-star luxury from THB 3,500–6,500+ · Pattaya rates swing a lot by season and weekday vs. weekend, and can be much higher in high season and on long weekends

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Pattaya hotel?
faq.a: For weekdays out of season, 1–2 weeks ahead is enough · but for weekends, high season (November–February), long weekends, New Year and Songkran, good rooms — especially beachfront resorts and sea-view rooms — fill fast and prices jump, so book 2–4 weeks ahead or more

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking a Pattaya hotel?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) differ by promotion at any given time, so always open and compare all 3 before booking — each review page in this guide has price-comparison links, which can save you hundreds to over a thousand baht per night on higher-priced rooms

faq.q: ❓ How do I get around Pattaya with no metro?
faq.a: Pattaya has no metro · the main way around town is the songthaew (red truck) looping along Beach Road and Pattaya 2nd Road from THB 10 · Grab and motorbike rental are also handy · From Bangkok it's about a 2-hour drive or van/bus, from U-Tapao Airport (UTP) around 40 minutes, and from Suvarnabhumi about 1.5–2 hours

faq.q: ❓ Coming to Pattaya with kids — where should we stay?
faq.a: Pick a resort with a water park or pools for kids and family rooms · Centara Grand Mirage has an on-site Lost World water park and rooms that sleep several kids, on Wong Amat Beach · Somerset Pattaya has large rooms with kitchens and a pirate-themed water park, opposite the mall · InterContinental Pattaya Resort has 3 pools and a Kids' Club on a quiet private beach
